title: Heaps
summary: A **heap** keeps one priority item near the top while the full collection stays only partly ordered.
refresher: A **heap** is useful when code repeatedly needs the next smallest or largest item. The root is quick to read, while insert and remove repair the parent-child rule.

blocks.prompt: What should a heap trace watch first?
choices: The state that proves the next move
The final button the user clicks
The color of the code editor
blocks.why: Watch the root and one child comparison first. If that comparison is wrong, later heap operations cannot be trusted.

blocks.prompt: Which debugging habit fits heaps best?
choices: Trace one small state change before trying a larger input
Start with the largest hidden case
Change the data structure after each failed test
Ignore the saved state and read only the final answer
blocks.why: A heap bug is easiest to find when one parent-child comparison is visible. The whole tree is too much to debug at once.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Heap code often breaks when it treats the array as fully sorted. Siblings can appear in either order; parent-child priority is the contract.
